title: Elwynn Forest
body: Elwynn Forest is the green heartland of the kingdom of Stormwind, a country of tall hardwoods, rushing rivers, quiet lakes and farmland made rich by frequent rain. Stormwind City stands in its northwestern hills, and from its gates the road runs south to Goldshire, the largest of the forest towns. The land remembers war. In the First War the orcish Horde marched through these woods, overran Goldshire and destroyed Northshire Abbey before reducing the capital to ruins, and only after the Second War did the people return to rebuild. Today the danger is quieter but it is everywhere. With much of the Stormwind Army fighting in distant lands, a thin line of marshals, deputies and guards must hold the forest against kobolds swarming its mines, Riverpaw gnolls on the western border, murlocs creeping up the eastern streams and the red-masked thieves of the Defias Brotherhood, whose camps are scattered all through the forest. The marshals now deputize any volunteer willing to help.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Elwynn_Forest (terrain, First War, Goldshire falls, Northshire Abbey destroyed, resettling after the Second War)
npc_text 2286 (Deputy Rainer: bulk of the army abroad)
quest 83 description (Defias camps pocketed throughout Elwynn)
notes: Converted: the Defias taking gold from Elwynn's mines dropped from the opening, since the schedule (quest 123) reveals it; it is told in 1229 and in parts of 1206, 1211, 1217, 1228 and 1232. The Defias are now placed in camps across the forest (quest 83). No parts. npc_text 2286 and 50016 reread: nothing from later builds. Scourge attack on Goldshire (3.0 event) left out on purpose.

title: Northshire Valley
body: Northshire Valley lies behind a wall and border gates northeast of Goldshire, a sheltered vale of farms and vineyards gathered around Northshire Abbey. The Knights of the Silver Hand had made it fairly safe, but that peace is fraying. A clan of kobolds has infested the woods north of the abbey, and sick young wolves, which the hunter Eagan Peltskinner believes were driven here out of Duskwood, prowl the slopes while livestock goes missing. Worse, a gang of thieves in red bandanas has appeared across the river to the east, calling itself a brotherhood. Marshal McBride and his deputies enlist every willing hand they can find.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Elwynn_Forest (Northshire east of Stormwind behind a wall, Goldshire southwest of Northshire)
quest 3100 reward text (Silver Hand made this place fairly safe)
page_text 209-211 (McBride's reports: kobolds, thieves, wolves from Duskwood, missing livestock)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Removed 'long' from the Silver Hand claim (quest 3100 says only that they made the place fairly safe).

title: Northshire Abbey
body: Northshire Abbey was founded by clerics of the Holy Light who came south from Lordaeron, and it has long served the people and soldiers of Stormwind. Orcs destroyed it in the First War, though refugees carried its sacred tomes out of the ruins, and in the Second War Cho'gall's Twilight's Hammer clan made it their headquarters. Afterward Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild it and gathered clerics, priests and paladins into the Brotherhood of Northshire. Today the abbey trains new defenders of the realm: warriors and paladins drill within its halls, mages and priests study in its library wing, and Brother Neals keeps the stores of food and wine from the bell tower.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Northshire_Abbey (founding, First War, Twilight's Hammer headquarters, Faol and the Brotherhood of Northshire, recruitment and training center)
page_text 2291 (Faol helped reform the Brotherhood of Northshire)
page_text 2439, 2445, 2463, 2465 (trainers in the abbey and its library wing)
quest 3905 description (Brother Neals manages food and drink, in the bell tower)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Reworded Faol's role: the wiki calls the Brotherhood a new order, page_text 2291 says he helped reform it, so the body no longer says founded.

title: Echo Ridge Mine
body: North of the abbey the hills rise to Echo Ridge, where Northshire's own mine cuts into the rock. Kobolds have claimed it. They first camped in the woods nearby, and Marshal McBride's scouts soon found the infestation larger than anyone had guessed, with kobold workers and laborers digging through the tunnels, candles perched on their heads. The marshal warns that every day the vermin are left in peace, they gain a firmer foothold in the valley. Clearing the mine is among the first duties he gives the volunteers who answer Northshire's call.
sources: page_text 209 (kobolds north of the abbey and in Echo Ridge Mine)
page_text 15 (candles the kobolds wear on their heads)
DB spawns: Kobold Worker 257 and Kobold Laborer 80 around -8700,-150
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. The larger infestation at Echo Ridge is McBride's premise for quest 15 (its description), not an outcome. verified

title: Northshire Vineyards
body: East of the abbey, across the river, lie the Northshire Vineyards, whose grapes were once the pride of Stormwind. Milly Osworth was in the middle of her harvest when the Defias Brotherhood moved in, and she fled leaving her buckets of grapes among the vines, afraid that if the thieves did not steal them, the guards chasing them would trample them. Defias thugs still loiter among the rows. Nearby, in a shack across the bridge, the cutthroat Garrick Padfoot has gathered a gang of thugs around him and has preyed on farmers and merchants for weeks, boasting that the land belongs to the Brotherhood now.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Elwynn_Forest (vineyards once the pride of Stormwind)
creature_text 103 (This land belongs to the Defias Brotherhood now)
DB spawns: Defias Thug 38 x71 and Garrick Padfoot 103 at -9056,-461
notes: Converted lightly, no parts: Garrick Padfoot put in the present tense, so the opening no longer reads as if his raids were over; his end is told in 1227 part 2. creature_text 103 reread: nothing from later builds. verified

title: Goldshire
body: Goldshire is the largest town in Elwynn after the capital, a crossroads where the roads from Stormwind and Northshire meet those running on toward Westfall and Redridge. Gnolls from Redridge once attacked it and were driven off by the Stormwind Army, and in the First War it was among the last towns to fall to the Horde. Rebuilt after the Second War, it is now Marshal Dughan's headquarters. At its heart stands the Lion's Pride Inn, whose keeper Farley promises rest to the tired and cold. Travelers gather there: the Redridge trader Remy 'Two Times', the apothecary William Pestle, and once Stalvan Mistmantle, who lodged there seeking work as a tutor after abandoning his post as headmaster in Moonbrook.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Goldshire (roads, Gnoll War, last towns to fall in the First War, rebuilt with Turalyon's support)
quest 107 description (William Pestle staying at the Lion's Pride Inn)
page_text 18 (Stalvan lodging at the Lion's Pride Inn after abandoning his Moonbrook post)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Stalvan's stay at the inn is kept: like Westfall's Moonbrook (4010) it tells only where he lodged after leaving his post, nothing of the Duskwood chain's outcome. npc_text 50017 reread: nothing from later builds. Stalvan was a headmaster seeking a tutor's post, not yet a tutor (page_text 18); road layout made general (wiki gives the roads, not that Goldshire sits just south of the junction).

title: Fargodeep Mine
body: Fargodeep Mine lies almost due south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure homesteads. The kobold trouble is not confined to Northshire: Marshal Dughan has reports that Fargodeep too has become a haven for the creatures. Kobold tunnelers and miners dig through its shafts, a brute called Narg the Taskmaster lurks among them, and so does a kobold with a mouthful of gold teeth. The kobolds carry gold dust and fat wax candles out of its depths, and traders in Goldshire pay well for both.
sources: quests 47, 60 (gold dust, large candles; Remy and William Pestle in Goldshire)
DB spawns: Narg the Taskmaster 79 at -9733,115, Goldtooth 327 at -9746,88, Kobold Tunneler 475
notes: Converted: the gold-toothed kobold with the widow's necklace (Billy's claim) moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 87, whose description tells it); the Defias gold and the months without miners moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 123: the schedule is read on accepting 123, Dughan's remark comes at its turn-in). The scouts' confirmation (quest 62 reward) dropped: the opening now gives Dughan's reports (quest 62 description); his reaction is told in 1228 part 1. Goldtooth kept in the opening as a spawn. verified

parts.body: The mine also holds a widow's treasure. Young Billy Maclure, after a slip of the tongue, swears he only saw old Auntie Bernice's lost necklace lying near Fargodeep, where a big, gold-toothed kobold snatched it up and ran with it into the mine.

The kobolds are not the only ones taking from Fargodeep. A schedule carried by Riverpaw gnolls shows the Defias Brotherhood gathering gold from the Elwynn mines and sending it to its headquarters in Westfall, though, as Marshal Dughan exclaimed on reading it, the kingdom has had none of its own people working the mines for months.

title: The Stonefield Farm
body: The Stonefield Farm lies west of Fargodeep Mine in southern Elwynn, home to a large and quarrelsome family. Ma Stonefield guards her vegetables from the Brackwells' enormous prize sow, the widowed Auntie Bernice bakes pork belly pies and mourns a necklace she has lost, Homer Stonefield sells fruit to passersby, and Gramma Stonefield keeps the house, trusted by her grandson to find a way where no one else can. The family is locked in a bitter feud with the Maclures to the east, which is hard on young Tommy Joe, who lingers by the river west of the farm, pining for Maybell Maclure.
sources: quests 106, 111 (feud, Tommy Joe at the river, Gramma)
quest 62 (mine between the Stonefield and Maclure homesteads)
notes: Converted lightly, no parts: the husband's lucky trinket is quest 87's reward text (Bernice gives it away when the necklace comes back), so it left the opening and is told in 1231 part 4; Bernice now mourns her lost necklace (quest 85). Gramma line narrowed to what quest 111 says (Tommy Joe trusts her to find a way).

title: The Maclure Vineyards
body: East of the Stonefields, beyond Fargodeep Mine, stand the Maclure Vineyards, where Joshua Maclure works as the family's vintner. The Maclures keep up their long feud with the Stonefields, but not every Maclure shares the grudge. Young Maybell Maclure has given her heart to Tommy Joe Stonefield and calls herself cursed, since she cannot see him without crossing her own kin. Then there is young Billy Maclure, a hungry and slippery boy whom old Auntie Bernice accuses of taking her necklace, and who cannot seem to remember anything useful until someone brings him a pie.
sources: quest 106 (Stonefield Farm due west of the Maclures)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Billy's want of a pie is what he says on meeting him (quest 85 reward, 86 description); what he then tells is in 1231 part 3. verified

title: Jerod's Landing
body: Jerod's Landing is a boat landing on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River, south of Goldshire where the forest meets the Duskwood border. It no longer serves honest trade. The Defias Brotherhood has seized it, and a Defias dockmaster, who carries the Brotherhood's shipping schedule, now directs a crew of dockworkers on the riverbank. Through the landing the thieves move stolen goods out of reach of the marshals, carried down from Redridge and bound for their holdings in Westfall.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Jerod's_Landing (boat landing on the Nazferiti, Defias Dockmaster, smuggling stolen goods from Redridge to Klaven's Tower in Westfall)
DB spawns: Defias Dockmaster 6846 at -9959,-132 (about map 48,87) and Defias Dockworker 6927 x3
creature_loot_template: Defias Dockmaster drops Defias Shipping Schedule 7675
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Dockmaster carries a single shipping schedule (loot, no page text), not guarding schedules. Smuggling route (Redridge to Westfall) is from the wiki, which lists the Defias Dockmaster as Classic content. Checked: one clause reordered so the shipping schedule belongs to the dockmaster.

title: Westbrook Garrison
body: Westbrook Garrison guards Elwynn's western border, a barracks and guard tower just past the bridge over a small brook on the road to Westfall. Deputy Rainer, who holds it, has far too few men. He cannot believe the officials in Stormwind sent the bulk of the army abroad while thieves slip over from Westfall and gnolls press in from east and west. His pleas to Goldshire for soldiers bring only volunteers. The garrison's quartermasters arm whoever will fight, a morale officer keeps spirits up, and a wanted poster outside calls for the death of the gnoll Hogger.
sources: creature_template 1645, 1249 quartermasters, 955 Sergeant De Vries <Morale Officer>
gameobject 68 Wanted Poster beside Rainer, starts quest 176
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. npc_text 2286 reread: nothing from later builds. verified

title: Forest's Edge
body: Forest's Edge is the wild southwestern corner of Elwynn, where the woods run down to the Westfall border. Packs of Riverpaw gnolls have made camps here, south of the Westbrook guard tower, in greater numbers than the garrison can handle alone, and the Stormwind Army rewards those who bring back their painted armbands. The fierce Gruff Swiftbite roams among them, and above them all looms Hogger, a huge gnoll who has overpowered every attempt at his capture.
sources: DB: Hogger 448 spawn has areaId 60; Gruff Swiftbite 100 spawns near -9988,609
notes: Converted: the Defias schedule carried by the gnolls moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 123, started from the dropped schedule, which is when its contents are read). Armband bounty softened to match quest 11 (the army will commend helpers).

parts.body: The gnolls do not act alone. Some of them, Gruff Swiftbite and even Hogger among them, carry a Defias schedule for the gold taken from Elwynn's mines, a sign that the Riverpaw pack and the Brotherhood are working together.
sources: creature_loot_template: Gold Pickup Schedule 1307 drops from Riverpaw Runt, Riverpaw Outrunner, Gruff Swiftbite, Hogger

title: Crystal Lake
body: Crystal Lake lies just east of Goldshire, a bright stretch of water in the heart of the forest and an easy walk from the Lion's Pride Inn. It is no longer a peaceful spot. Murlocs crowd its shores, and their streamrunners prowl the banks, making the lake dangerous for anyone careless enough to wander close. Some of the creatures carry crystal kelp, a frond that usually grows in the ocean, and the apothecary William Pestle prizes it for brewing an invisibility liquor.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Crystal_Lake (directly east of Goldshire, crawling with murlocs)
DB spawns: Murloc 285 x35 and Murloc Streamrunner 735 x21 around -9480,-350
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Removed the link to the eastern-stream murlocs (Remy's report is about eastern Elwynn; the Stone Cairn murlocs are a separate group) and the Riverpaw gnolls (no gnoll spawns anywhere near the lake; the earlier averages were misleading).

title: Tower of Azora
body: Along the road running east from Goldshire rises the Tower of Azora, where the high mage Theocritus presides. Servants of Azora tend its halls, a clothier and a dealer in arcane goods trade within, and its shelves hold histories of distant lands. Within the tower rests the Eye of Azora, a device Theocritus developed to gaze upon the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge, lair of his bitter rival, the warlock Morganth. The two towers are locked in a constant feud, each spying on the other by magical means.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tower_of_Azora (road from Goldshire to Eastvale, Eye of Azora, constant feud, mutual spying)
quest 178 description (High Mage of Tower Azora)
DB spawns: Servant of Azora 1949 x10, Morley Eberlein <Clothier>, Dawn Brightstar <Arcane Goods>
gameobject 175760 Rise of the Blood Elves in the tower
quest 76 description (east along the road to the tower)
DB: Eye of Azora gameobject 19548 inside the tower
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Dropped 'small company of mages' (unsupported) and 'at the top' (the Eye's position is not documented); location tied to quest 76; feud no longer called long-standing.

title: Jasperlode Mine
body: Jasperlode Mine lies in the foothills north of the Tower of Azora, the more distant of the two Elwynn mines that Marshal Dughan wants scouted. Rumor in Goldshire already says kobolds infest it, and the traders there send anyone seeking gold dust or wax candles to its tunnels. Kobold geomancers and miners, with the trapper Ruklar, hold its approaches, and deeper inside the kobolds share the dark tunnels with mine spiders, among them a great spider known as Mother Fang.
sources: quests 47, 60 descriptions (rumors of kobolds at Fargodeep and Jasperlode)
DB spawns: Kobold Geomancer 476 x8, Kobold Miner 40, Ruklar the Trapper 60 at -9251,-708, Mother Fang 471 at -9052,-621, Mine Spider 43 x8 around -9038,-587
notes: Converted, no parts: the scout's report and Dughan's curse (quest 76 reward text) left the opening, which now gives Dughan's wish to have the mine scouted (76 description) and the Goldshire rumors (quests 47, 60); the report is told in 1228 part 2. verified

title: Stone Cairn Lake
body: Stone Cairn Lake spreads across northeastern Elwynn, ringed around a single large island. Murlocs have built a village on its shores, and they are aggressive and cunning enough to be a real danger. A few days ago two soldiers from the eastern bridge, Rolf and Malakai, went north along the river to investigate, and they have not come back. The lake was once a safe place for pilgrims, but the island at its center is now held by Defias rogue wizards.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Stone_Cairn_Lake (ring shape around an island, murloc tribe, rogue wizards, formerly a safe pilgrimage site)
quest 35 reward text (aggressive and at least semi-intelligent)
DB spawns: Murloc Lurker 732 and Murloc Forager 46 near Rolf's corpse; Defias Rogue Wizard 474 x18 on the island
notes: Converted: Malakai's body moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 37, turned in at the body) and Rolf's remains to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 45, at his corpse); the opening keeps the two guards missing, as quest 37 presents it, and gives only their first names, since the full names are read from the medallions. Pilgrimage claim moved from the island to the lake, as the wiki has it.

parts.body: Malakai was found by the water north along the river, his body half eaten and stripped of nearly everything. Only a medallion lying nearby, etched with the words Footman Malakai Stone, told who he had been. From the body, webbed footprints led east along the lakeshore toward the murloc village.

The footprints ended in the murloc village, where Rolf's remains lay. Around the dead man's neck hung a metal medallion inscribed Footman Rolf Hartford. Neither of the two guards sent out from the bridge will be coming home.

title: Heroes' Vigil
body: At the center of the island in Stone Cairn Lake stands Heroes' Vigil, a ring of stones around the Stone of Remembrance. The monument honors all who fell defending Stormwind, above all in the First War, when the orcs sacked Goldshire and the lands around it. Defias rogue wizards now hold it. Two paladins, Gazin Tenorm and Henze Faulk, came here seeking proof that the Defias had slipped across the kingdom's borders, and when they attacked the wizards they were quickly overwhelmed by their spells. Henze held them off so that Gazin could escape.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Heroes'_Vigil (ring of stones, Stone of Remembrance, Rogue Wizards)
DB: gameobject 20923 at -9135,-1050; Henze Faulk 6172 at -9130,-984; Defias Rogue Wizard x18 on the island
notes: Converted: the Defias plan in the script (staging camp, reinforcements from Westfall) moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 1787, when the script is handed to Gazin; the script drops only for that quest), together with Henze's fall and return (1786 reward). The opening keeps Gazin's account (1786 description) and no longer calls it a plot. The script's closing boast was left out. Paladin quests 1786 and 1787 are class quests (QuestSortID -141, human only) used by no other file. npc_text 6062 reread: nothing from later builds. verified

parts.body: Henze Faulk fell holding off the wizards, but the Light brought him back, and the papers the Defias had been studying were taken from them at last. Their script lays out the plan: Heroes' Vigil, all but forgotten by the people and soldiers of Stormwind, is to become a base camp, and once it is ready, reinforcements will be moved in from Westfall and the Brotherhood's attacks staged from here.
sources: quest 1786 reward text (Henze fell and was brought back)
page_text 811 (Defias Script, item 6846, drops only for quest 1787)

title: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch
body: The Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in southeastern Elwynn was the Brackwell family's farm until bandits took it, and no one knows what became of the family. Their prize sow Princess remains, grown huge on vegetables stolen from the Stonefields, and trots about with a small entourage of pigs. The farm is now a Defias hideout, and here the young warlock Surena Caledon fled with the Defias bandit Erlan Drudgemoor, wearing a bloodstone choker her old master wants back.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Brackwell_Pumpkin_Patch (pre-Cataclysm: Brackwells' fate unknown, Defias control, Princess, Surena)
DB spawns: Princess 330 and Porcine Entourage 390 x2, Morgan the Collector 473, Surena Caledon 881, Erlan Drudgemoor 880 around -9806,-930
notes: Converted: the gold gathered here for the Collector moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 123, when the schedule is read). Erlan is a warrior-class NPC the wiki calls a bandit, so 'rogue' changed to 'bandit'.

parts.body: The hideout has a purpose. By a Defias schedule carried by the Riverpaw gnolls, gold from Elwynn's mines is gathered here twice a week, on Sundays and Wednesdays, for a Brotherhood agent known only as the Collector, until a party from the Defias headquarters in Westfall comes to take it away.

title: Eastvale Logging Camp
body: In eastern Elwynn, near the Redridge border, the Eastvale Logging Camp supplies the kingdom with lumber. Orders come steadily and deadlines are strict, so Supervisor Raelen frets when wolves and bears from the woods to the north chase her workers away from their chopped bundles. Sara Timberlain fashions armor for the forest's defenders, and at the stables Katie and Randal Hunter breed horses and teach riding, though only to those who have earned Stormwind's full trust. Just southeast of the camp stands the manor of the retired Marshal Haggard, once a noble family's summer cottage.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Marshal_Haggard (manor southeast of Eastvale, former Flintridge summer cottage)
page_text 20 (the Lord's summer cottage near Eastvale)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. npc_text 4859, 5855, 5861 reread: nothing from later builds. verified

title: Marshal Dughan
body: Marshal Dughan commands the Stormwind Army's forces in Goldshire and answers for the safety of the town and the forest around it. It is a thankless post. With the army fighting far away, he must make do with deputies and volunteers while kobolds fill the mines, gnolls and thieves press from the west, and new troubles arrive faster than he can answer them. He is a cautious man, unwilling to send scarce troops east on a merchant's word without a military report to back it. He has posted a generous bounty on the gnoll Hogger.
notes: Converted: Thomas's report of the two dead guards and Dughan's alarm moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 39, turned in to Dughan). npc_text 16211 reread: a general complaint about new troubles, nothing from later builds. Faction 1: Dughan uses faction template 12 (Stormwind), hostile to Horde.

parts.body: The military report came. Guard Thomas sent word from the eastern bridge that two of his men, Rolf and Malakai, had died at the murlocs' hands, and that his small force could not contain the creatures. Dughan took it hard: his defenses were already stretched thin, and he feared there would be fighting in Goldshire by the week's end.

title: Marshal McBride
body: Marshal Douglas McBride commands the Stormwind Army garrison at Northshire Abbey and the defense of the valley. With so many soldiers sent abroad, he depends on volunteers, and he sends each newcomer first against the kobolds in the northern woods and the Echo Ridge Mine. His careful written reports track the kobolds, the wolves driven out of Duskwood and the red-bandanaed thieves who have appeared in the valley, and they name one of the gang's leaders, Garrick Padfoot, whom he hopes to bring to justice soon.
sources: page_text 209-212 (McBride's reports and commendation, signed Marshal Douglas McBride)
notes: Converted: the commendation that ends the Northshire chain moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 54, which hands over the documents). npc_text 4938 reread: nothing from later builds. Faction 1: McBride uses faction template 12.

parts.body: Volunteers who see the work in Northshire through do not leave empty handed. McBride sends them south with his signed commendation, awarding them Deputy status with the Stormwind Army for serving the valley with eagerness and distinction, and with his reports for Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, who will find them useful in the wider forest.

title: Hogger
body: Hogger is a huge gnoll who prowls the woods of southwestern Elwynn as chieftain of the Riverpaw pack. Since the Third War the Riverpaw have raided farms and villages across the forest, armed and guided, it is said, by the Defias Brotherhood. Hogger himself has overpowered every attempt to capture him, and the Stormwind Army now offers a generous bounty for proof of his death, paid by Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, who counts the beast a real pain for himself and his men.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hogger (pre-Cataclysm: Riverpaw chieftain, raids after the Third War, Defias weapons and leadership)
notes: Converted: Dughan's headache line (quest 176 reward text) moved out of the opening. Added part 1, Hogger's death (KILL 448 or QUEST_DONE 176), and part 2, Dughan's relief on the bounty (QUEST_DONE 176 only). The opening now ends with the request text (a real pain for me and my men). creature_text 448 reread: battle cries only. Faction 0: the KILL trigger is open to both factions. Hogger Hill name, his capture and the Stockade are Cataclysm and left out.

parts.body: Hogger has fallen at last. The great gnoll who had overpowered every attempt at his capture was hunted down in the woods of southwestern Elwynn and slain, and the Riverpaw pack lost the chieftain who had led its raids.

When the huge claw was laid before Marshal Dughan, he laughed with relief. He had begun to think no one would ever take the monster down, he admitted, and he paid the bounty gladly, for the beast had been giving him a headache the size of Blackrock Spire.

title: Morgan the Collector
body: Morgan, whom the Brotherhood calls the Collector, is a Defias agent in Elwynn Forest. He keeps to the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in the southeast of the forest, the farm the bandits took from the Brackwell family, and lives there among the thieves who have made it their hideout, while the family's enormous sow Princess roots through the fields around them. His title hints at some business he keeps for the Brotherhood, though what he collects, and for whom, is written only in the Brotherhood's own papers.
sources: quest 123 description (the Collector resides near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch)
quest 88 description (Princess at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch)
DB: Morgan the Collector 473 (faction 17, Defias) at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch
notes: Converted: the Stonemason ring (a cross-zone spoiler of Westfall's quest 141 reveal) left the opening. It is told only in part 3 (QUEST_DONE 147, whose reward text names the guild), and only as Dughan's open question. Checked: the schedule (gold from the mines, twice a week, the Westfall party, the ring) also left the opening and is part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 123, when the schedule is read), since the opening also unlocks from KILL 473 alone, which reveals none of it, and the rest of the file holds the Defias mine gold behind quest 123. Part 2, his death (KILL 473 or QUEST_DONE 147), no longer mentions the mine shipments. The ring loots only for quest 147, so a Horde killer earns part 2 alone. The schedule's -EVC signature, its craftsmen line and the ring's -EVC engraving are left out.

parts.body: Those papers turn up among the Riverpaw gnolls. By the schedule they carry, gold from the Elwynn mines is gathered at the pumpkin patch twice a week, on Sundays and Wednesdays, and handed to the Collector, until a party from the Brotherhood's headquarters in Westfall comes to take it from him. He is to be known by an engraved ring, given to him by the master who wrote the schedule.
sources: page_text 79, 250 (The Collector's Schedule, item 2223, given on accepting quest 123)
creature_loot_template: Gold Pickup Schedule 1307 drops from Riverpaw gnolls

parts.body: The Collector will collect nothing more. He was hunted down among the Defias who hold the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and slain there, and the Brotherhood lost the agent it had kept at the farm.
sources: DB: Morgan the Collector 473 at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch

parts.body: The ring taken from his body, engraved for years of service, puzzled Marshal Dughan. It is a membership ring of the old Stonemasons' Guild of Stormwind. Why a lowly thief would wear an artisan's guild ring, and why the Defias are collecting money from the kingdom's mines, the marshal cannot say, though he hopes the answers will come one day.
sources: quest 147 reward text (Stonemason's Guild membership ring)
item 2239 The Collector's Ring (engraving; loots only for quest 147)

title: Theocritus
body: Theocritus is the high mage of the Tower of Azora, a scholar who prefers to watch his enemies from afar. Through the Eye of Azora, a device of his own making, he spies on his rival Morganth, a vicious warlock of great power who rules the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge. Seeing the warlock is not enough: Theocritus means to study his thoughts and learn his future plans. He has also spent months of research on the enchanted pendants through which Morganth speaks to his Shadowhide gnolls, trying to send his own voice through them.
notes: Converted: the Scythe of Elune and the peril to Redridge and Stormwind (quest 249, Redridge's reveal, told in redridge.json 4418 and 4424) removed from the opening, and so was the pendant experiment's result (quest 178 reward text, Redridge 4424 part 1). The opening keeps his spying (94) and his pendant research (178 description). No parts: his quests 94, 178, 248, 249 are Redridge's triggers. TALK 313 kept. Faction 1: Theocritus uses faction template 12. The Morganth chain itself is in Redridge (QuestSortID 44), so no Story entry here.

title: Marshal Haggard
body: Marshal Haggard once led men of the Stormwind Guard and now lives in retirement in a manor just southeast of the Eastvale Logging Camp, among the weapons of a long career. His eyes are failing. On a dark night the Defias rogue Dead-tooth Jack came to him wearing a Stormwind tabard, and Haggard, taking him for Marshal Dughan, handed over his old marshal's badge before the thief laughed and ran off to his camp somewhere to the south. The manor holds older secrets too: a chest upstairs, already there when Haggard moved in, holds a bundle of old parchments he gave up reading as his sight failed, among them a faded page from the journal of Stalvan Mistmantle.
sources: quest 1666 description (retired, collected a lot of gear)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Marshal_Haggard (former leader of the Stormwind Guard, manor southeast of Eastvale, eyesight)
DB: Dead-Tooth Jack 6093 at -9769,-1566 (south of the manor)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Haggard's tale of Dead-tooth Jack is quest 1667's premise; the chest of journal pages is what he says on offering Duskwood's quest 75, and tells nothing of how the Stalvan chain ends. Faction 1: Haggard uses faction template 12 and quest 1667 is Alliance only. Checked: the chest line put in the present tense (the pages are still there for a newcomer); it names only where a clue lies, nothing of the Duskwood chain's outcome (quest 75 description).

title: Guard Thomas
body: Guard Thomas is posted to Elwynn's eastern bridge for the Stormwind Army, keeping watch over the road toward the Eastvale Logging Camp. From there he sees the forest's troubles firsthand: wolves and bears grown bold, and murlocs settling into the eastern streams, aggressive and at least half clever. A few days ago he sent two guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the river to investigate, and neither has returned. He must know what became of them to finish his report, and meanwhile he pays the army's bounty on murloc fins.
sources: quest 59 description (Eastvale beyond Guard Thomas' post)
notes: Converted: the guards' deaths and his warning to Goldshire moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 71, the medallions delivered to him; 39 is offered on that turn-in). The opening keeps them missing (quest 37). npc_text 50018 reread: nothing from later builds. Faction 1: Thomas uses faction template 12.

parts.body: The medallions of Rolf Hartford and Malakai Stone came back to the bridge without them. Both men had died at the murlocs' hands, confirming Thomas's fears, and he sent word to Goldshire that the murlocs of eastern Elwynn could not be contained by the few troops he had.

title: Remy 'Two Times'
body: Remy, known as 'Two Times' for his habit of saying everything twice, is a trader from Redridge who came to Goldshire looking for business. He buys the gold dust that kobolds carry out of the mines, promising the best price in town, and pays in coin along with tokens from certain associates of his. Remy is also the first to raise the alarm about murlocs swimming up the eastern streams, scaring off fish and attacking gentle folk, though Marshal Dughan, more worried about gnolls and bandits, is not convinced the creatures are a danger.
sources: npc_text 50017 (from Redridge, looking for business, repeats himself)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Remy_%22Two_Times%22 (nickname from repeating the ends of his sentences, merchant from Redridge)
notes: Converted: the confirmation of his warning moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 39, Thomas's report reaching Dughan); the opening keeps Dughan's doubt as Remy tells it (quest 40 description). npc_text 50017 reread: nothing from later builds. Nickname origin confirmed by the wiki. Faction 1: Remy uses faction template 12.

parts.body: Remy was right. Dughan respected him as a merchant but would not move troops on a merchant's word, and only a military report from Guard Thomas at the eastern bridge, telling of two guards slain by the murlocs, convinced the marshal that the danger was real.

title: The Defense of Northshire
body: Northshire's guards are stretched thin, so Deputy Willem stands outside the abbey enlisting anyone willing to defend their home. Marshal McBride sends each volunteer first to cull the kobold vermin in the northern woods, then to the Echo Ridge Mine, where his scouts report the infestation is larger than feared. The hunter Eagan Peltskinner asks for the diseased young wolves to be put down before their sickness spreads, and the deputy offers rewards for the red bandanas of a new gang calling itself the Defias Brotherhood, and a bounty on Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat who hides with his thugs near the vineyards. Milly Osworth needs her abandoned grapes rescued from those same thieves before they are stolen or trampled.
notes: Converted: the Echo Ridge skirmish moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 21), Garrick Padfoot's end to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 6), the saved grapes and Brother Neals's joy to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 3905), and the commendation that ends the chain to part 4 (QUEST_ACCEPT 54, which hands over the documents). Entry triggers unchanged. Faction 1: all quests AllowableRaces 1101 (Alliance).

parts.body: The skirmish at Echo Ridge earned McBride's respect and the gratitude of the Stormwind Army. Kobolds may yet linger in the mine, the marshal admits, but he will marshal others against them, and he has further tasks for those who proved themselves in its tunnels.

Garrick Padfoot plagues Northshire no longer. The cutthroat was found at his shack near the vineyards despite the thugs he had gathered around him, and his head was brought to Deputy Willem, who called it a great service to Elwynn and paid the bounty.

Milly's harvest was saved, and her grape manifest went to Brother Neals in the bell tower, who keeps the abbey's food and drink. Neals had nearly despaired when he heard that brigands had overrun the vineyards, but his faith in the Light never wavered, and now the abbey has grapes for more wine.

When the valley is safer, McBride signs commendations naming his best volunteers deputies of the Stormwind Army, for serving Northshire with eagerness and distinction, and sends them south along the road past the border gates to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, charged now with the protection of the wider forest.

title: Kobolds in the Mines
body: Kobolds have spread from Northshire across Elwynn. Marshal Dughan, already troubled by gnolls and thieves, has reports that the Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire has become a haven for them, and he wants it scouted, and after it the more distant Jasperlode Mine in the eastern foothills. Not everyone in Goldshire sees only trouble. The apothecary William Pestle wants the large wax candles the kobolds wear on their heads, to ship to his brother Morgan's shop in Stormwind, and Remy 'Two Times' pays well for the gold dust they carry.
notes: Converted: the two scouting reports moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 62) and part 2 (QUEST_DONE 76); the Defias gold moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 123). The opening now gives Dughan's reports and his wish to have both mines scouted (62 and 76 descriptions). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Fargodeep proved as bad as the reports. Kobolds have made the mine their haven, and Dughan, hearing it, wondered aloud whether dragons would be next. He ordered the patrols near the mine increased and at once found another task for his scout.

Jasperlode was no better. Kobolds hold that mine too, and Dughan cursed at the news: the situation, he said, was worsening by the minute, and he only wished his scout had brought him good news for once.

The kobolds' gold dust hinted at a deeper theft. A schedule found on the Riverpaw gnolls showed the Defias Brotherhood gathering gold from these same mines for its headquarters in Westfall, though Stormwind has had none of its own miners working them for months. Someone in the forest, it seemed, was quietly receiving the kingdom's gold.

title: The Collector
body: The trail begins with a scrap of paper carried by Riverpaw gnolls: a schedule of Defias gold collection from the Elwynn mines to the Brotherhood's headquarters in Westfall. Twice a week the gold is gathered at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, to be handed to an agent known only as the Collector, recognized by an engraved ring his master gave him. A party from headquarters then takes the gold away, and every brother is reminded to play his part with discipline and discretion. Such a find belongs in the hands of Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.
sources: page_text 79, 250 (The Collector's Schedule, item 2223, given on accepting 123)
creature_loot_template: item 1307 Gold Pickup Schedule from Riverpaw Runt, Outrunner, Gruff Swiftbite, Hogger
notes: Converted: the opening is the schedule as read on accepting 123. Dughan's astonishment and his order moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 123; 147 is offered on that turn-in). The Collector's death and the Stonemason ring moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 147, whose reward text names the guild); the ring is given only as Dughan's open question, so it does not get ahead of Westfall's reveal (quest 141). The schedule's signed closing line about former craftsmen is left out for the same reason. Faction 1: quests 123 and 147 are Alliance only.

parts.body: Marshal Dughan was astonished, for the kingdom has had none of its people working the Elwynn mines for months. He had heard of this Collector, but not whom he served. Whoever is taking that gold is stealing from the kingdom, he reasons, and he orders the Collector brought to justice, along with the ring named in the schedule, which might tell whom the thief works for.

The Collector was found at the pumpkin patch and slain, and he will collect from the Elwynn mines no more. His ring raised more questions than it answered. It is a membership ring of the old Stonemasons' Guild of Stormwind, and Dughan cannot say why a lowly thief would wear an artisan's guild ring, or why the Defias would be collecting money from the kingdom's mines. He can only hope the answers will come.

title: Murlocs in the East
body: Remy 'Two Times' is the first to warn of murlocs swimming up the streams of eastern Elwynn, scaring off fish and attacking gentle folk. Marshal Dughan, busy with gnolls and bandits, is not convinced, and without a military report he will not send more troops east. That report must come from Guard Thomas, posted for the past week at the eastern bridge, who knows the state of the land there better than anyone. At the bridge Thomas also pays the Stormwind Army's bounty on murloc fins.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup (40, and 35's description). Parts follow the chain: 1 Thomas's confirmation and the missing guards (QUEST_DONE 35), 2 Malakai's body (QUEST_DONE 37), 3 Rolf's remains (QUEST_DONE 45), 4 the report and Dughan's fear (QUEST_DONE 39, which follows 71, the medallions delivered to Thomas). Entry triggers unchanged. Bounty no longer presented as a result of the report (quest 46 is offered independently). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: The rumors were true. Murlocs have settled in and around the eastern streams, Thomas reports, aggressive and at least half clever, and no one knows why they came. Worse, a few days ago he sent two guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the river to investigate, and they have not returned.

Malakai's half-eaten body lay by the water, stripped of nearly everything but a medallion bearing his name, Footman Malakai Stone. From there webbed footprints led east along the shore of Stone Cairn Lake, toward a murloc village barely visible in the distance.

Rolf's fate ended in that village. His remains lay among the murlocs, a metal medallion inscribed Footman Rolf Hartford still around his neck, and with both medallions in hand there was no more doubt about what had become of the two guards Thomas had sent out.

Thomas's report reached Goldshire: the murlocs could not be contained by the troops at the bridge. The deaths of Rolf and Malakai troubled Dughan deeply, for his defenses were already stretched thin, and he warned that if things did not improve, there would be fighting in Goldshire by the week's end.

title: The Stonefields and the Maclures
body: Two farming families of southern Elwynn, the Stonefields and the Maclures, have long been bitter enemies, and their children pay the price. Maybell Maclure loves Tommy Joe Stonefield and sends him a secret letter, for she cannot see him without crossing her kin. Tommy Joe, aching to be with her, turns to his Gramma, who sees no end to the feud but hopes the pair might have a little time together, and she writes for help to the apothecary William Pestle in Goldshire, whom she has not seen in years. Not every tale between the farms is so tender. Auntie Bernice Stonefield blames young Billy Maclure for her missing necklace, and Ma Stonefield wants the Brackwells' greedy sow Princess dead before she eats another crop.
notes: Converted: Pestle's plan moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 112), Maybell's escape to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 114), Billy's confession to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 87, after the pie, 84), the returned necklace and the husband's trinket to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 87). Princess's fate stays untold, as before. Entry triggers unchanged. Letters made singular (quest 106). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: William Pestle's heart went out to the young lovers, and he found a way: an invisibility liquor that would let Maybell slip away from the Maclure Vineyards unseen. He needed only crystal kelp, a frond that usually grows in the sea but that the murlocs of Crystal Lake sometimes gather.

The liquor reached Maybell. She felt guilty deceiving her family, she confessed, but her feelings for Tommy Joe were too strong to ignore, and she meant to drink it at the first chance and sneak away to her love.

Billy denied everything at first. He was no thief, he said, though he might remember who was if someone fed him, and only one of Bernice's own pork belly pies loosened his tongue. After a slip about dropping the necklace himself, he swore he had seen a big, gold-toothed kobold snatch it up and run into Fargodeep Mine.

The necklace came home to Auntie Bernice, and the old widow was overjoyed. In thanks she gave away a keepsake of her husband's, a trinket he always called lucky, though he forgot to take it with him on his last campaign.

title: The Western Border
body: With the bulk of Stormwind's army sent abroad, Westbrook Garrison on Elwynn's western border is struggling. Word reaches Goldshire of growing gnoll and thief activity, but Marshal Dughan has no soldiers to spare and can send only volunteers to Deputy Rainer. Riverpaw gnolls have settled in the woods south of the garrison's tower in numbers greater than the guards can handle, and another pack haunts the land near Stone Cairn Lake. The army commends anyone who brings back their painted armbands. Looming over them all is Hogger, a gnoll so huge that he has overpowered every attempt at capture, and whose claw is worth a generous bounty in Goldshire.
notes: Converted: the Defias schedule among the gnolls moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 123); Hogger's death added as part 2 (QUEST_DONE 176). The second gnoll pack near Stone Cairn Lake added from quest 11's description. npc_text 2286 reread: nothing from later builds. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only (176 starts from the Wanted Poster object).

parts.body: The gnolls are more than a nuisance. Some of them carry a Defias schedule for the gold stolen from Elwynn's mines, a sign that the Riverpaw pack and the Brotherhood work hand in hand, and the trail it opens leads to the Collector at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch.

Hogger fell at last. When his huge claw reached Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, the marshal confessed he had begun to think no one would take the monster down, and he paid the bounty with relief, for the beast had been giving him a headache the size of Blackrock Spire.
